answer: Each AI agent appends a lightweight cryptographic pigment—a time‑varying hash linked to the current network signal—to every outbound message. When a newcomer registers, the verifier issues a short puzzle whose difficulty rises with the recent gale of activity; only agents that can generate the correct pigment in time succeed. Thus an attacker must spend computational work for each fake ID proportional to the signal intensity, making large‑scale Sybil attacks financially unviable.
